Paraphrased: authors must check any AI-produced material for accuracy and plagiarism before submission; an AI tool may be cited as a source only if the author has independently verified the content; authors must acknowledge AI-generated intellectual content, including text, images, videos, audio, graphics and computer code; language polishing of human text needs no acknowledgment only if it changes no meaning and adds no intellectual content; AI-generated data that simulates or emulates a process must be clearly labelled as AI-generated; when an AI tool is the subject of the article, releasing source code and curated data is recommended; editors and referees must not use AI tools that breach review confidentiality. The Conference Author Center page links to these principles.

introspection_log: Method: re-derived every checkable claim independently rather than trusting the report's URLs. Structured sources (Crossref, OpenAlex, GitHub REST, PyPI JSON) were parsed as JSON with python. IEEE PDFs (2026 APC list, Article Sharing and Posting Policies, PSPB Operations Manual amended 25 June 2026) were downloaded with curl and parsed with pypdf/pdfplumber. HTML pages (CIBCB 2026 and 2027 sites, IEEE CIS calendar, IEEE Access, IEEE conference Author Center, OSF help, Zenodo help and developer docs, PLOS, JOSS, ReScience, eLife, Frontiers, bioRxiv FAQ, GitHub docs) were fetched raw with curl and a browser user agent, tags stripped, and read directly, avoiding model summarisation. WebFetch (model-summarised, exact-sentence prompts) was used only where curl was blocked or pages are JS-rendered: embs.org JBHI/TNSRE (curl 403), IEEE journal Author Center policy pages, IEEE Open AI guideline, Zenodo enable-repository/about-records, computer.org CSDL (JS-only, no content). WebSearch was not usable (session search budget exhausted), so no secondary aggregators were consulted. Key adversarial results: (1) the report's claim that no official CIBCB 2027 page exists and that the CIS calendar is blocked is false; the calendar returns 200 to curl with a browser UA (only WebFetch gets 418) and links to an official 2027 site. (2) The report never read the PSPB Operations Manual, whose AI principles section has several obligations missing from the report. (3) JBHI submits via Atypon ReX, not ScholarOne. (4) The TCBB 'tcbbio' DOI pattern is not universal for vol 22. (5) ReScience also accepts reproductions. (6) The Sharing PDF itself names only arXiv/TechRxiv for preprints. Limits: TCBB scope and sponsors, magazine/book AI pages, Zenodo concept DOI and private-repo support, OSF cost, the IEEE approved not-for-profit server list, CIBCB 2027 fees, and the exact TNSRE OA start date remain unverified. additional_findings: IEEE PSPB Operations Manual (amended 25 June 2026), Introduction, 'IEEE Principles of Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence in Publishing', pp. 5-6: authors are responsible for all content; AI output must be checked for accuracy and plagiarism before submission; AI tools may be cited as sources only if independently verified; acknowledgment covers AI-generated text, images, videos, audio signals, graphics and computer code; language polishing needs no acknowledgment only if meaning and intellectual content are unchanged; AI-generated data simulating a process must be labelled; code and curated data release recommended when an AI tool is the subject. For NeuroSem's agent case study (AI tool as subject), this recommends releasing agent-task code and curated data. https://pspb.ieee.org/images/files/files/opsmanual.pdf

PSPB manual 8.2.1.B.5: when submitting, authors must disclose prior publication or active consideration elsewhere, and must notify IEEE immediately if they submit to a non-IEEE publication while under IEEE review. 8.2.1.A.4: each part essential to the main conclusions must be the responsibility of at least one author. https://pspb.ieee.org/images/files/files/opsmanual.pdf

PSPB manual 8.1.9: preprints may be posted on personal sites, employer servers, or approved not-for-profit third-party servers; the IEEE Publishing Ethics Team maintains the approved list and PSPB approves hosts. The list itself was not retrieved, so bioRxiv's status remains unknown. https://pspb.ieee.org/images/files/files/opsmanual.pdf

CIBCB 2027 (official): 24th IEEE CIBCB, Bocconi University, Milan, Italy; PhD competition/hackathon 31 Aug 2027; main conference 1-3 Sep 2027; special sessions 29 Jan 2027; tutorials 19 Feb 2027; full papers 2 Apr 2027 (at most 8 pages); notification 21 May 2027; short papers 11 Jun 2027 (at most 2 pages); camera-ready and early registration 25 Jun 2027; deadlines 23:59 AoE; EasyChair (TBC); at least one author expected to present on site; accepted and presented papers submitted to IEEE Xplore. https://attend.ieee.org/cibcb-2027/important-dates/ ; https://attend.ieee.org/cibcb-2027/call-for-papers/ ; https://cis.ieee.org/conferences/conference-calendar

CIBCB 2027 scope keeps 'Modelling, Simulation, and Optimization of Biological Systems' and 'Surrogate Modeling and Representation', now under 'AI/CI in Computational Systems Biology'; a new 'Ethics, Fairness, and Biases' topic appears; neuroscience and software testing are still not named. https://attend.ieee.org/cibcb-2027/scope-topics/

Tool note: the IEEE CIS calendar returns HTTP 418 to WebFetch but 200 to curl with a browser user agent. Other IEEE 418 'blocks' in the evidence base may also be WebFetch-specific and worth retrying with curl. https://cis.ieee.org/conferences/conference-calendar

CIBCB 2026 site inconsistency: Important Dates gives early registration 30 Jun 2026, the Registration page uses 3 Jul 2026 as the early-bird cutoff; the 24% VAT applies only when an invoice is requested. https://cibcb2026.dib.uth.gr/important-dates/ ; https://cibcb2026.dib.uth.gr/registration/

IEEE Xplore about-journal page for TCBB (punumber 8857) still carries the old 'IEEE/ACM' title in its HTML title and meta description on 2026-09-13, while Crossref and the 2026 APC list use the IEEE-only title. Cite the title printed on each article's own metadata. https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/xpl/aboutJournal.jsp?punumber=8857

OpenAlex merges old and new TCBB ISSNs into one source record (1545-5963, 1557-9964, 2374-0043, 2998-4165). OpenAlex bibliometrics for 'TCBB' therefore span both titles. https://api.openalex.org/sources/issn:2998-4165

TNSRE OA switch editorial: 'TNSRE Is Flipping to Full Open Access', D. P. Ferris and K. McArthur, IEEE TNSRE vol 28 no 7, July 2020, p. 1510, DOI 10.1109/tnsre.2020.3004668. https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1109/tnsre.2020.3004668

2026 IEEE APC list page allowances: TNSRE has no overlength charge and allows 30 pages in its first manuscript-type column; JBHI allows 8 regular pages with $250/$350 overlength. Relevant if a long methods paper is planned. https://journals.ieeeauthorcenter.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/IEEE-Article-Processing-Charges-List.pdf

IEEE Access warns that articles found to contain fabricated content, including nonexistent references, are promptly rejected. This reinforces the handoff's no-fabricated-citations rule for any AI-assisted drafting. https://ieeeaccess.ieee.org/authors/preparing-your-article/

IEEE conference Author Center: when AI is used for grammar editing, leave the reference section out of the tool's input and always double-check AI results. https://conferences.ieeeauthorcenter.ieee.org/author-ethics/guidelines-and-policies/submission-policies/

OSF nuance for M8: a submitted registration and its documents cannot be modified, but OSF has a formal 'Update' process that appends updates (48-hour admin approval) without altering the original. Embargoed registrations can be shared for blinded review via anonymised view-only links. A public registration cannot be re-embargoed. https://help.osf.io/article/158-create-a-preregistration

JOSS AI disclosure must name the tools, say where and how they were used, and state that humans reviewed and validated all AI-assisted output and made the core design decisions. JOSS updated its criteria in 2026 to emphasise human design thinking and demonstrated research impact. https://joss.theoj.org/about

bioRxiv FAQ: generative-AI use should be detailed in the manuscript like other computational methods, and authors remain accountable for accuracy, integrity and originality. https://www.biorxiv.org/about/FAQ

ReScience C: authors may not submit replications of their own or close collaborators' research; reproductions (Rp) and failed replications/reproductions are accepted; no publication fees. https://rescience.github.io/faq/ ; https://rescience.github.io/write/

Frontiers in Neuroinformatics: 'Methods' and 'Technology and Code' are A-type articles (CHF 3,150); fee support for World Bank low and lower-middle income countries. https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neuroinformatics/for-authors/publishing-fees

Zenodo developer REST docs expose a 'conceptrecid' field and an 'all_versions' query parameter, indicating a concept-record grouping of versions. An explicit concept-DOI statement was not retrieved. https://developers.zenodo.org/
JBHI manuscript submission is through Atypon ReX: https://ieee.atyponrex.com/journal/jbhi-embs (link found on https://www.embs.org/jbhi/).
